Overall, Neighbor 3 is another mutagenic reference whose structural and physicochemical differences still favor the query being not mutagenic.

Neighbor 4 is a non-mutagenic analog, and several of its differences are mixed, but the overall comparison still stays on the non-mutagenic side. Neighbor 5 is nearly the same local case as Neighbor 4, so it behaves the same way. So Neighbor 5 also fits the non-mutagenic outcome.

Neighbor 6 is another non-mutagenic analog, and here the comparison is especially informative because the query is less donor-rich and lacks some polar functional groups. Those changes reduce donor capacity and remove polar motifs that can influence exposure and reactivity patterns. The query also has one alkene while the neighbor has none (delta +1), which is the main feature that leans the other way, and it has one fewer rotatable bond than the neighbor (16 vs 17, delta -1). Putting the six neighbors together, the three mutagenic references are all outweighed by the query’s higher flexibility, larger surface area, higher logD, higher sp3 character, and extra carboxylic ester content, while the three non-mutagenic references mostly align with the query’s lower ring burden and less aromatic character. On balance, the local analog evidence supports option (A): is not mutagenic.
